source.title: The Galois action on symplectic K-theory
source.authors: Tony Feng, Soren Galatius and Akshay Venkatesh
readSections: Published version (open access, CC BY 4.0; PDF SHA-256 5da9a2b28d13b2b22a262a81650188025020d92238ec2b47404d177ef91d7b4d, fetched from link.springer.com 22 September 2026), read in full: §1 Introduction, §2 K-theory recollections, §3 Symplectic K-theory, §4 CM abelian varieties, §5 CM classes exhaust KSp, §6 the Galois action, §7 the main theorem, §8 families and stable homology, Appendix A (construction of the Galois action)

arXiv 2007.15078v3 TeX source (SHA-256 45353b7d89c63be6836e3df0550e4fdc68765b730b79d9dbb41c1324bad2e13d) used as a reading aid; a word-level diff against the published text shows layout changes and four corrections in the published §8/Appendix A (∂y = p^k x, F_p, KSp_n(Z; Z/p^k), a typo)

summary: Feng, Galatius and Venkatesh compute the action of Aut(C) on the p-adic symplectic K-theory of Z, which comes from the moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties. For odd p, KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) is an extension of Z_p(2k − 1) (via the Hodge map c_H) by K_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) with trivial action, and the extension is the universal one for Γ = Gal(H_{p^∞}/Q) (Theorem 7.8; also for the unramified-outside-p group with a split decomposition group, Theorem 7.10, and for Bott-inverted KSp in all degrees, Theorem 7.14). The proof identifies KSp(Z; Z/q) with K(Z)^{(+)} ⊕ ku^{(−)} (Theorem 3.5, via Karoubi), shows that classes from CM abelian varieties with cyclotomic multiplication exhaust it (Proposition 5.1), and computes the Galois action on them by the main theorem of complex multiplication (Theorem 6.6), matching the resulting cocycle with the tautological one in relative Galois homology (§7.3). Consequences: divisibility of Chern numbers of families of abelian varieties over Q by primes dividing Bernoulli numerators (Theorem 8.1). Appendix A constructs the action on the spectrum through p-completed étale homotopy types of a Γ-object in simplicial schemes over Q. The atlas plans the K-theory, Hermitian K-theory, Thomason and norm-residue inputs, class field theory, and CM theory; it has nothing on symplectic K-theory's Galois action, CM classes, universal extensions in relative Galois homology, Bott-inverted symplectic K-theory, or the Galois action on étale homotopy types of moduli. Routes: a Part II of ArithmeticKTheory for the paper's own mathematics, sources for MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7 (Thomason), ArithmeticKTheory N.6 (explicit Bott-inverted K-theory) and GN.6 (Karoubi), and the étale-homotopy parts of the Appendix coalesced into the EtaleHomotopyTypes candidate. Theorem 8.1 needs p > max n_j (the edge case p = max n_j is unproved), and the proof of Theorem 8.4 asserts a loop-space splitting that fails in general.

items.name: Number fields, cyclotomic and CM fields, class groups, symplectic groups and group homology
items.statement: Rings of integers O_E, class groups π_0 Pic(O_E), cyclotomic fields Q(ζ_q) and their integers O_q = Z[ζ_q], CM fields; the symplectic group Sp_{2g}(Z) of the standard form Σ(x_{2i−1}y_{2i} − x_{2i}y_{2i−1}); homology of discrete groups with coefficients in a module.
items.note: Mathlib has NumberField.RingOfIntegers, ClassGroup, CyclotomicField/IsCyclotomicExtension, NumberField.IsCMField, Matrix.symplecticGroup and groupHomology. It has no CM orders, CM types, Hilbert class fields or stable homology of Sp_{2g}(Z).

items.name: Algebraic K-theory spectra of symmetric monoidal groupoids
items.statement: For a symmetric monoidal groupoid 𝒞 an infinite loop space machine gives a spectrum K(𝒞) and a group completion |𝒞| → Ω^∞K(𝒞), inducing the Grothendieck group on π_0; for a ring R, K(R) := K(𝒫(R)) with K_i(R) = π_i BGL_∞(R)^+ for i > 0, graded-commutative products for commutative R, and the adjoint ring maps Σ^∞_+|𝒞| → K(𝒞).
items.note: StableHomotopyKTheory H.4 plans group completion of symmetric monoidal groupoids (Γ-spaces), H.5 spectra and suspension spectra; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2:plus the ring and plus-construction model.

items.name: Mod q homotopy and p-completion of spectra
items.statement: π_i(E; Z/q) := π_i(E ∧ S/q) with the long exact Bockstein sequence; p-adic groups K_i(Z; Z_p) := lim_n K_i(Z; Z/p^n), valid because K_*(Z; Z/p^n) are finite; stable homotopy π^s_*(Y) = π_*(Σ^∞_+Y) of an unpointed space.
items.note: StableHomotopyKTheory H.6 plans E/m, the Bockstein sequence and p-completion with lim¹. The ring structure on S/q for q = p^n > 4 (and its failure of associativity for q = 3, Remark 2.19) is used but not planned.

items.name: Adams operations and the involution ψ^{−1}
items.statement: Adams operations ψ^k on K_*(R) for commutative R, with ψ^{−1} induced by M ↦ Hom_R(M, R) and f ↦ (f^∨)^{−1}; for odd q it splits mod q groups into ±1-eigenspaces; on π_{2k}(ku) it acts by (−1)^k.
items.note: SchemeKTheoryOperations S.6 plans λ- and Adams operations.

items.name: Quillen's localization sequence and K-theory of finite fields (Lemma 2.10)
items.statement: Dévissage and localization give fibre sequences K(F_p) → K(Z) → K(Z′) and K(F_p) → K(O_q) → K(O′_q) (Z′ = Z[1/p], O′_q = O_q[1/p]); with K_i(F_p; Z/q) = 0 for i ≠ 0 this gives that Z → Z′ induces isomorphisms on mod-q K-theory except in degree 1, where K_1(Z′; Z/q) ≅ Z/q ⊕ K_1(Z; Z/q), and likewise for O_q → O′_q.
items.note: GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.3 plans dévissage and localization, ArithmeticKTheory N.2 the localization sequence (N.8 the case Z[1/p]), KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1 Quillen's computation.

items.name: Norm residue theorem and the comparison with Bott-inverted K-theory (Proposition 2.9)
items.statement: For X = Spec Z′ or Spec O′_q the localization K_i(X; Z/q) → K^{(β)}_i(X; Z/q) is an isomorphism for i > 0 and injective for i = 0 (in fact bijective, Lemmas 2.11, 2.14); for Spec Z and Spec O_q it is an isomorphism for i ≥ 2. The proof compares the motivic and Thomason spectral sequences, using the norm residue theorem (Voevodsky–Rost).
items.note: MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5 plans the norm residue theorem and M.7 the Quillen–Lichtenbaum comparison with an explicit degree range.

items.name: Topological K-theory ku and Bott periodicity
items.statement: The connective complex K-theory spectrum ku (of the topological groupoid of Hermitian C-vector spaces), π_*(ku) = Z[Bott] in nonnegative degrees, π_*(ku; Z/q) = Z/q[Bott], and ψ^{−1} acting by (−1)^k on π_{2k}.
items.note: RefinedTraceMethods RT.4:topological plans topological complex K-theory and Bott periodicity.

items.name: Symplectic K-theory of Z
items.statement: SP(Z) is the symmetric monoidal groupoid of free Z-modules with a perfect skew-symmetric pairing under orthogonal sum; KSp(Z) := K(SP(Z)), KSp_i(Z; Z/q) := π_i(KSp(Z); Z/q), KSp_i(Z; Z_p) := lim_n KSp_i(Z; Z/p^n); equivalently KSp_i(Z; Z_p) = lim_g π_i(BSp_{2g}(Z)^∧_p) (§1.2), with the Hurewicz map KSp_i(Z; Z_p) → H_i(Sp_∞(Z); Z_p).
items.note: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.6 plans higher hermitian K-spaces of exact categories with duality, including alternating forms; KSp(Z) is GW^{-s}_{cl}(Z) in the nine-author notation.

items.name: Complex uniformization of polarized abelian varieties
items.statement: A complex torus V/Λ with a positive definite Hermitian form whose imaginary part is a perfect Z-valued symplectic form on Λ is a principally polarized abelian variety (Riemann forms; Mumford, Abelian varieties, §I.2).
items.note: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5 plans complex uniformization with polarization.

items.name: CM fields, CM orders and CM types
items.statement: A CM field is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field, a CM algebra a product of such, a CM order an order stable under conjugation; a CM type Φ ⊂ Hom(E, C) contains one embedding from each conjugate pair, equivalently E ⊗ R ≅ C^Φ.
items.note: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.0 plans orders in CM fields and CM types; Mathlib has NumberField.IsCMField.

items.name: The main theorem of complex multiplication
items.statement: For σ ∈ Aut(C) and a CM abelian variety with CM type Φ, σ(A) is described by the reflex norm / Taniyama element: in Milne's form (Thm. 4.2 of 'The fundamental theorem of complex multiplication'), for E Galois with Hilbert class field H and embeddings w_τ extending τ with w_{τc} = w_{cτ} = cw_τ, the ideal class changes by the class whose Artin symbol is Σ_{τ∈Φ} w_{στ}^{−1}σw_τ ∈ Gal(H/E)^{ab}.
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V5 plans CM abelian varieties and CM reciprocity; ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.2 its ideal/idele dictionary.

items.name: Hilbert class fields, narrow class fields and the Artin map
items.statement: Class field theory identifies π_0 Pic(O_E) with Gal(H̃/E) for the Hilbert class field H̃ by the Artin symbol, and ({±1}^S × fractional ideals)/(principal signed ideals) with the Galois group of the narrow Hilbert class field of a totally real field; H_q is the maximal p-power subextension of the Hilbert class field of K_q.
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layers 11 and 13 plan global Artin reciprocity and the (narrow) Hilbert class fields.

items.name: Chebotarev density for number fields
items.statement: Every conjugacy class of a finite Galois extension of number fields is the Frobenius of infinitely many (a positive density of) primes.
items.note: Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10 plans Dirichlet-density Chebotarev.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre and Poitou–Tate duality
items.statement: The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for profinite group extensions, and Poitou–Tate duality for S-integers (with compactly supported cohomology defined as a cone), used for transfers in étale cohomology of O′_q and Z′.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.15, p. 247; Remark 7.17, p. 295
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2 and R02.4 plan these.

items.name: Non-vanishing of K_{4k−2}(Z)_p and Vandiver's conjecture
items.statement: K_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) (≅ Ker c_H) is non-zero exactly when p divides the numerator of ζ(1 − 2k) (Mazur–Wiles with the norm residue theorem; first case k = 6, p = 691); Vandiver's conjecture at p is equivalent to p ∤ h(Q(ζ_{p^n})^+) for all n (Washington, Cor. 10.7).
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5 plans the classical main conjecture and L3 Vandiver's condition; ArithmeticKTheory N.7 relates Bernoulli numerators to K-theory.

items.name: Lemma 2.3: the Bott element in the stable homotopy of BZ/q
items.statement: For odd q there is a unique β ∈ π^s_2(B(Z/q); Z/q) whose image under π^s_2 → π^s_1 → H_1(BZ/q; Z)[q] = Z/q is 1 (the Hurewicz map π^s_2(BZ/q; Z/q) → H_2(BZ/q; Z/q) being an isomorphism), and Z/q[β] → π^s_*(BZ/q; Z/q) is a split injection of graded rings (for q = p^n > 4), split by the map to π_*(ku; Z/q) of the line bundle of j : Z/q → S^1, a ↦ e^{2πia/q}, which sends β to Bott; replacing j by j^a multiplies the image by a (Remark 2.4).

items.name: Picard groupoids and the map to K-theory
items.statement: For commutative R, Pic(R) ⊂ 𝒫(R) is the symmetric monoidal groupoid of rank-1 projectives under ⊗, with π_0 = H^1(R; G_m), π_1 = R^×; π^s_*(BR^×) ⊗ Z[π_0 Pic(R)] ≅ π^s_*(|Pic(R)|) (2.4), and Σ^∞_+|Pic(R)| → K(R) is a map of ring spectra (2.5).

items.name: Bott elements in mod q K-theory and Bott-inverted K-theory
items.statement: A primitive q-th root of unity ζ ∈ R^× gives β ∈ K_2(R; Z/q) (the image of β ∈ π^s_2(BZ/q; Z/q)); intrinsically β : μ_q(R) → K_2(R; Z/q) (2.5). Bott-inverted K-theory K^{(β)}_*(X; Z/q) = K_*(X; Z/q)[β^{−1}], defined for all Z[1/p]-schemes via Thomason's canonical β^{p−1} ∈ K_{2p−2}(Z; Z/p) and its lifts, or as the homotopy of K(X) ∧ T for the telescope T of an Adams v_1 self-map Σ^m S/q → S/q, m = 2p^{n−1}(p − 1) (Remark 2.8); K^{(β)}_*(Z; Z_p) := lim_n.

items.name: Thomason's étale descent spectral sequence for Bott-inverted K-theory
items.statement: For a Z[1/p]-scheme X (mild hypotheses) there is a convergent spectral sequence E^2_{s,t} = H^{−s}_et(X; μ_q^{⊗(t/2)}) ⇒ K^{(β)}_{t+s}(X; Z/q), concentrated in s ≤ 0, t ∈ 2Z, arising as a hyperdescent spectral sequence, compatible with Adams operations ψ^a (a prime to p), which act on E^2_{s,t} by a^{t/2}; it is natural for transfers (Blumberg–Mandell §10).
items.note: Thomason, Algebraic K-theory and étale cohomology (1985).

items.name: Lemmas 2.11 and 2.14: Bott-inverted K-theory of O′_q and Z′
items.statement: For all k ∈ Z and odd q: K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O′_q; Z/q)^{(+)} ≅ H^2(O′_q; μ_q^{⊗2k}), ^{(−)} ≅ H^0(O′_q; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}); K^{(β)}_{4k}(O′_q; Z/q)^{(+)} ≅ H^0(O′_q; μ_q^{⊗2k}), ^{(−)} ≅ H^2(O′_q; μ_q^{⊗(2k+1)}); K^{(β)}_{2k−1}(O′_q; Z/q) ≅ H^1(O′_q; μ_q^{⊗k}) with ψ^{−1} = (−1)^k; K_i(O′_q; Z/q) → K^{(β)}_i is an isomorphism for i ≥ 0 and K_i(O_q; Z/q) → K^{(β)}_i for i = 0 or i ≥ 2. The same statements hold with Z′ and Z in place of O′_q and O_q (with period p^{n−1}(p − 1) in k).
items.note: The ±-splitting of the even-degree extensions uses ψ^{−1}; injectivity plus a count of orders gives degree 0.

items.name: Corollary 2.12: the Picard group in Bott-inverted K-theory
items.statement: The map π_0(Pic O_q) ⊗ μ_q(O_q)^{⊗(2k−1)} → K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O_q; Z/q)^{(+)}, [L] ⊗ ζ^{⊗(2k−1)} ↦ β(ζ)^{2k−1}·([L] − 1), is a Gal(K_q/Q)-equivariant isomorphism (after reducing π_0 Pic mod q); its degree-0 part is the mod-q étale Chern class c_1.
items.note: The identification with c_1 is quoted as well known (the preprint FGV outlined a proof).

items.name: Proposition 2.15: transfers on coinvariants
items.statement: For odd q, the transfer K_*(O′_q; Z/q) → K_*(Z′; Z/q) induces isomorphisms (K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O′_q; Z/q)^{(+)})_{Gal(K_q/Q)} ≅ K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z′; Z/q)^{(+)} and (K^{(β)}_{4k}(O′_q; Z/q)^{(−)})_{Gal(K_q/Q)} ≅ K^{(β)}_{4k}(Z′; Z/q)^{(−)}.
items.note: Proof by naturality of Thomason's spectral sequence for transfers, Poitou–Tate duality and a relative Hochschild–Serre sequence; H^0_c(O′_q; μ_q^{⊗(1−t)}) = 0.

items.name: Proposition 2.17: the transfer as a map of Galois homology
items.statement: For all k ∈ Z there is a commutative square whose horizontal maps are isomorphisms: H_1(H_q/K_q; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) ← π_0(Pic O_q) ⊗ μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)} → K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O_q; Z/q)^{(+)} (Artin map and Corollary 2.12) over H_1(H_q/Q; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) ≅ K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q)^{(+)}, the vertical maps being i_* (surjective) and the transfer; the same holds without Bott inversion for k ≥ 1. Also H_1(H_q/Q; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) ≅ H_1(Gal(H_q/Q), ⟨c⟩; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) (Remark 2.18).
items.note: Coinvariants of Gal(K_q/Q) via Hochschild–Serre and the 'center kills' argument with complex conjugation.

items.name: The Betti and Hodge maps
items.statement: c_B : KSp(Z) → K(Z) from the forgetful functor SP(Z) → 𝒫(Z); c_H : KSp(Z) → ku in the homotopy category, from SP(Z) → SP(R^top) ← 𝒰(C^top), the second arrow (L, h) ↦ (L_R, Im h) being an equivalence because U(g) ⊂ Sp_{2g}(R) is a homotopy equivalence. With Q_p coefficients c_H is the Chern character of the Hodge bundle, and KSp_i(Z; Z_p) ⊗ Q_p is Q_p(2k − 1) for i = 4k − 2 and 0 otherwise (1.3).

items.name: Karoubi's splitting of symplectic K-theory after inverting 2
items.statement: KSp_n(Z)[1/2] ≅ K_n(Z)[1/2]^{(+)} ⊕ {}_{−1}W_n(Z)[1/2] with the Witt groups Z[1/2] for n ≡ 2 (mod 4) and 0 otherwise; on spectra there is a fibre sequence K(Z)_{hC_2} → KSp(Z) → τ_{≥0}L^{−s}(Z) (Hebestreit–Steimle, Cor. 8.3.5), which after inverting 2 becomes K(Z)[1/2]^{(+)} → KSp(Z)[1/2] → τ_{≥0}L^{−s}(Z)[1/2], split by c_B, the first map being the hyperbolic construction.
items.note: Karoubi, Théorie de Quillen et homologie du groupe orthogonal (1980); the nine-author Hermitian K-theory papers; Hebestreit–Steimle.

items.name: Theorem 3.5 and Corollary 3.6: symplectic K-theory of Z
items.statement: For odd q = p^n, (c_B, c_H) : KSp_i(Z; Z/q) → K_i(Z; Z/q)^{(+)} ⊕ π_i(ku; Z/q)^{(−)} is an isomorphism; in particular KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) ≅ H^2(Z′; μ_q^{⊗2k}) ⊕ Z/q for k ≥ 1. For odd p and i > 0, KSp_i(Z; Z_p) is 0, 0, K_i(Z; Z_p) ⊕ Z_p, K_i(Z; Z_p) for i ≡ 0, 1, 2, 3 (mod 4). On spectra KSp(Z)[1/2] ≃ K(Z)[1/(1+ψ^{−1})] × ku[1/(1−ψ^{−1})] (Remark 3.9).
items.note: The proof uses Karoubi's splitting and Proposition 3.8.

items.name: Proposition 3.8: the Hodge map is non-zero mod p
items.statement: For every k ≥ 1, KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/p) → π_{4k−2}(ku; Z/p) ≅ Z/p induced by c_H is non-zero; hence KSp_{4k−2}(Z) → π_{4k−2}(ku) ≅ Z becomes surjective after inverting 2.
items.note: Proved via Proposition 5.2 (a CM class).

items.name: Bott-inverted symplectic K-theory and K(1)-localization
items.statement: KSp^{(β)}_i(Z; Z/q) := π_i(KSp(Z); Z/q)[v_1^{−1}] = π_i(KSp(Z) ∧ T) and KSp^{(β)}_i(Z; Z_p) := lim_n; (c_B, c_H) gives KSp^{(β)}_i(Z; Z/q) ≅ K^{(β)}_i(Z; Z/q)^{(+)} × π_i(K; Z/q)^{(−)} for all i ∈ Z (Corollary 3.10); these agree with π_i(L_{K(1)}KSp(Z); Z/q) and π_i(L_{K(1)}KSp(Z)) (Remark 3.11, via Ravenel Thm. 10.12).

items.name: Hermitian and skew-Hermitian Picard groupoids
items.statement: For O with involution and a rank-1 projective ω with involution ι, 𝒫(O, ω, ι) has objects (L, b) with L rank-1 projective and b : L ⊗ L̄ → ω an isomorphism with b(x ⊗ y) = ι(b(y ⊗ x)). For a CM field E: 𝒫^+_E = 𝒫(O, O, conjugation), a symmetric monoidal groupoid, and 𝒫^−_E = 𝒫(O, 𝔡^{−1}, −conjugation) (skew-Hermitian forms valued in the inverse different); tensor bifunctors 𝒫(ω) × 𝒫(ω′) → 𝒫(ω ⊗ ω′) (4.5) give an action of 𝒫^+_E on 𝒫^−_E, making π_0 𝒫^−_E a π_0 𝒫^+_E-torsor. (L, b) ↦ (L_Z, −Tr^E_Q b) is a functor 𝒫^−_E → SP(Z) (4.3)–(4.4); all objects have automorphism group U_1(O) = {x : xx̄ = 1}, so |𝒫^−_E| ≃ BU_1(O) × π_0 𝒫^−_E.

items.name: CM abelian varieties from skew-Hermitian modules
items.statement: For (L, b) ∈ 𝒫^−_E the CM type Φ_(L,b) = {j : Im(j b(x, x)) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ L_R} makes ⟨x, y⟩_b = −2i Σ_{j∈Φ} j(b(x, y)) a positive definite Hermitian form on L_R with imaginary part −Tr b, so L_R/L_Z is a principally polarized abelian variety ST(L, b) with O ⊂ End respecting the polarization in the sense (a, 1)^*ℒ = (1, ā)^*ℒ. This gives a functor ST : 𝒫^−_E → 𝒜_g(C) through SP(Z) (4.6), an equivalence onto 𝒜^O_g(C) (Remark 4.5), and for positive definite (X, q) ∈ 𝒫^+_E, ST((L, b) ⊗ (X, q)) ≅ ST(L, b) ⊗_O (X, q) (Serre's tensor construction; Remark 4.6). The functor 𝒜_g(C) → SP(Z), A ↦ (H_1(A(C); Z), c_1(ℒ)), gives Σ^∞_+|𝒜_g(C)| → KSp(Z) (4.1)–(4.2) with 𝒜_g(C) discrete.

items.name: Proposition 4.7: enough skew-Hermitian modules over a cyclotomic field
items.statement: For every CM structure Φ on O_q and L ∈ Pic(O_q) there are (B_1, b_1), (B_2, b_2) ∈ 𝒫^−_{K_q} with [B_1][B_2] = [L][L̄]^{−1} in π_0 Pic(O_q) and Φ_(B_1,b_1) = Φ_(B_2,b_2) = Φ. The different of O_q is generated by q/(ζ_q^{q/p} − 1), and δ = (1 + ζ_q)^{q/p}·q/(ζ_q^{q/p} − 1) is a purely imaginary generator.
items.note: Checked by hand, including δ̄ = −δ.

items.name: Lemma 4.8: totally real primes with prescribed signs
items.statement: For every f : Hom(O_q^+, R) → {±1} there is a nonzero prime t ∈ O_q^+ with sgn j(t) = f(j) for all real embeddings j and tO_q = 𝔵𝔵̄ for a prime 𝔵 of O_q.
items.note: Chebotarev in H_q^+K_q/K_q^+, which is Gal(H_q^+/K_q^+) × Gal(K_q/K_q^+), with the narrow Artin map.

items.name: Proposition 5.2: the Hodge map on CM classes
items.statement: For (L, b) ∈ π_0 𝒫^−_{K_q} the class β^i[L, b] ∈ π^s_{2i}(|𝒫^−_{K_q}|; Z/q) maps under Σ^∞_+|𝒫^−| → KSp(Z) → ku to (Σ_{a∈(Z/q)^×, j_a∈Φ_(L,b)} a^i)·Bott^i, where j_a(ζ_q) = e^{2πia/q}; for every odd i some CM structure Φ makes this a generator of π_{2i}(ku; Z/q).
items.note: The restriction to the object (L, b) is the unitary representation ⊕_{j∈Φ} j|_{μ_q}. Checked: switching the element of Φ in {1, −1} changes the sum by ±2.

items.name: Corollary 5.4: the Betti map on CM classes
items.statement: The composite π^s_{4k−2}(|𝒫^−_E|; Z/q) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) → K_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q)^{(+)} sends β^{2k−1}·[(L, b)] to tr(β^{2k−1}·([L] − 1)), tr : K(O) → K(Z) the transfer; in particular tr(β^{2k−1}) = 0.

items.name: Proposition 5.1: CM classes exhaust symplectic K-theory
items.statement: For E = K_q the composite π^s_{4k−2}(|𝒫^−_{K_q}|; Z/q) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) is surjective for every k ≥ 1; the classes β^{2k−1}[(L, b)] generate.
items.note: Uses Theorem 3.5, Propositions 2.17, 4.7 and 5.2 and Corollary 5.4; checked the identity [L_1] + [L_2] = [L] − [L̄] + 2 in K_0(O_q).

items.name: Galois conjugation of complex varieties and of 𝒜_g(C)
items.statement: For σ ∈ Aut(C) and a C-scheme (X, φ), σ(X, φ) = (X, Spec(σ^{−1})∘φ); this gives a strict action of Aut(C) on the groupoid 𝒜_g(C) and on |𝒜_g(C)|, agreeing with the functor of points of 𝒜_g applied to Spec σ.

items.name: Proposition 6.1: the Galois-equivariant source surjects
items.statement: For all k ≥ 1 and odd q = p^n, π^s_{4k−2}(|𝒜_g(C)|; Z/q) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) is surjective whenever g ≥ φ(q)/2.
items.note: Stated as corrected; the paper states g ≥ φ(q) (true but not sharp) and reduces to g = φ(q) (sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 6.2: the Aut(C)-action on KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q)
items.statement: For every k ≥ 1 and odd q there is a unique action of Aut(C) on KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) making the maps π^s_{4k−2}(|𝒜_g(C)|; Z/q) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) equivariant for all g; the actions are compatible in q and give the action on KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p), and the spectrum-level action (Appendix A) also acts on KSp_{4k−1}.
items.note: Uniqueness from Proposition 6.1; existence from Appendix A.

items.name: Lemma 6.4: the Betti map and complex conjugation
items.statement: c_B : KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) → K_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) is equivariant for ⟨c⟩ ⊂ Aut(C), complex conjugation, with the trivial action on the target.

items.name: Theorem 6.6: the Galois action on CM classes
items.statement: For a Galois CM field E and σ ∈ Aut(C), the functor F_σ : 𝒫^−_E → 𝒫^−_E with ST∘F_σ ≅ σ∘ST acts on each fibre of π_0 𝒫^−_E → π_0 𝒫^−_{E⊗R} by tensoring with a class [(X, q)] ∈ π_0 𝒫^+_E depending on σ and the CM type, with Art(X) = class of Σ_{τ∈Φ} w_{στ}^{−1}σw_τ in Gal(H/E)^{ab} (6.3); for E = K_q, F_σ is Z/q[β]-linear on π^s_*(|𝒫^−|; Z/q).
items.note: Deduced from the main theorem of CM (Milne, Thm. 4.2) and the Serre tensor construction.

items.name: Categories of extensions with equivariant splitting and their universal objects
items.statement: For a group G, H ≤ G and a Λ[G]-module M, 𝒞_Λ(G, H; M) has objects (V, π, s) with π : V → M G-linear, s : M → V H-linear, π∘s = id_M and T = Ker π with trivial G-action; 𝒞_Λ(G; M) forgets s. The cocycle α(g, m) = g·s(m) − s(g·m) gives [α] : H_1(G, H; M) → T, an equivalence with Λ-modules under H_1(G, H; M), so the initial object has T^univ ≅ H_1(G, H; M) (Lemma 7.4); if H_0(H; M) = 0 = H_1(H; M) (resp. H_0(H; M) = 0) the forgetful functor to 𝒞_Λ(G; M) (resp. its H-split part) is an equivalence (Lemma 7.6). The same holds for profinite G with p-adically complete finitely generated modules (§7.4).
items.note: Definition 7.3 prints 's∘π = id_M' (sourceIssues).

items.name: Theorem 7.1: the Galois action mod q
items.statement: Let H_q be the maximal unramified abelian p-extension of K_q, G = Gal(H_q/Q) and c complex conjugation. (i) The Aut(C)-action on KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) factors through G. (ii) Ker(c_H) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) → μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)} (identified via Bott^{2k−1} ↦ ζ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) is an exact sequence of G-modules with trivial action on Ker(c_H), uniquely split ⟨c⟩-equivariantly by Ker(c_B). (iii) It is initial in 𝒞_{Z/q}(G, ⟨c⟩; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}) and in 𝒞_{Z/q}(G; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}): the cocycle is α(σ, x) = [σ ⊗ x] ∈ H_1(G, ⟨c⟩; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}).
items.note: Checked the cocycle computation (7.15)–(7.19), including the relations in C_1 modulo ∂C_2 and C_1(⟨c⟩).

items.name: Theorem 7.8 (Main theorem): the universal extension over Q
items.statement: For odd p, with Γ = Gal(H_∞/Q), H_∞ = ∪_n H_{p^n}: (i) c_H : KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) → Z_p(2k − 1) is surjective and Aut(C)-equivariant; (ii) its kernel (≅ K_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p)) is a finite p-group with trivial action; (iii) the action factors through Γ, the sequence Ker(c_H) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) → Z_p(2k − 1) is uniquely ⟨c⟩-split and is initial in 𝒞_{Z_p}(Γ, ⟨c⟩; Z_p(2k − 1)) and in 𝒞_{Z_p}(Γ; Z_p(2k − 1)).

items.name: Theorem 7.10: the universal property over the unramified-outside-p Galois group
items.statement: Let G = Gal(Q^{(p)}/Q) for the maximal extension unramified outside p (and ∞), and G_𝔭 the decomposition group of a prime 𝔭 of H_∞ fixed by c on each H_q (such exists since ℘(q) has odd order [H_q : K_q]). Ker(c_H) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) → Z_p(2k − 1) is uniquely G_𝔭-split, by Ker(c_B), and initial in 𝒞_{Z_p}(G, G_𝔭; Z_p(2k − 1)) and in 𝒞_{Z_p}(G; Z_p(2k − 1))^{G_𝔭-split}; equivalently the étale sheaf on Z[1/p] defined by KSp is the universal extension of Z_p(2k − 1) by a trivial sheaf split over Q_p (Remark 7.11). Via Lemmas 7.12–7.13 for Gal(H_q/Q)_𝔭 and G.
items.note: Remark 7.9 on Vandiver's conjecture is misstated (sourceIssues).

items.name: Theorem 7.14: universal properties of Bott-inverted symplectic K-theory
items.statement: For every k ∈ Z (including k ≤ 0), 0 → K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) → KSp^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q) → μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)} → 0 is initial in 𝒞_{Z/q}(Gal(H_q/Q), ⟨c⟩; μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}), and its Z_p-version is initial for Γ (with ⟨c⟩ or without) and for (G, G_𝔭); independently of the norm residue theorem (Remark 1.4, Remark 7.15).
items.note: For positive k via Proposition 2.9, for all k by v_1-periodicity.

items.name: §7.7: the Galois action on KSp_{4k−1}(Z; Z_p) is trivial
items.statement: Aut(C) acts trivially on KSp_{4k−1}(Z; Z_p) ≅ K_{4k−1}(Z; Z_p): π^s_{4k−1}(pt) → KSp_{4k−1}(Z; Z_p) (from S ↦ Z[S] ⊗ H) is surjective, since composed with c_B it is twice Quillen's surjection π^s_*(pt; Z_p) → K_*(Z; Z_p) ≅ K_*(F_ℓ; Z_p) (ℓ a topological generator of Z_p^×), and it factors through an elliptic curve over Q. Poitou–Tate gives H_2(G, G_𝔭; Z_p(2k − 1)) ≅ K_{4k−1}(Z; Z_p) (Remark 7.17).
items.note: The footnote writes χ_cyc^{2k−1} for the twist 2k (sourceIssues).

items.name: Stable homology of Sp_{2g}(Z): stability, rational structure and the Galois action
items.statement: H_i(Sp_{2g}(Z); Z_p) is independent of g for g ≥ 2i + 5 (Charney, Cor. 4.5), Aut(C) acts through the identification with H^*(𝒜_{g,C}) and étale cohomology; H_*(Sp_∞(Z); Q_p) ≅ Q_p[x_2, x_6, x_10, …] with Aut(C) acting on x_{4k−2} by χ_cyc^{2k−1}, and the Hurewicz map KSp_i(Z; Z_p) → H_i(Sp_∞(Z); Z_p) identifies KSp ⊗ Q_p with the primitives.

items.name: Theorem 8.4: stable homotopy as indecomposable homology
items.statement: For a connected spectrum E with finitely generated homotopy groups and X = Ω^∞E, the composite π_i(E) ⊗ Z_p → H_i(X; Z_p) → H_i(X; Z_p)_Ind of the Hurewicz map and the quotient by integral decomposables I² + Σ_k β_k(I_k²) (I, I_k the augmentation ideals of H_*(X; Z_p), H_*(X; Z/p^k), β_k the Bocksteins) is an isomorphism in degrees 1 ≤ i ≤ 2p − 2. Example 8.3: for X = RP^∞ the integral indecomposables are Z/2 in degrees 2^i − 1 and 0 otherwise. Lemma 8.5: for connected H-spaces X, Y of finite type, H_*(X; Z_p)_Ind ⊕ H_*(Y; Z_p)_Ind ≅ H_*(X × Y; Z_p)_Ind.
items.note: Stated as corrected: the paper assumes E p-complete, which fails as written for ordinary Z_p-homology, and its proof asserts a loop-space splitting of τ_{≤2p−2}X that fails for E = ΣS^∧_p (sourceIssues). Example 8.3 and Lemma 8.5 checked by computer in small cases.

items.name: (8.2): symplectic K-theory is indecomposable stable homology
items.statement: With integral decomposables of H_*(Sp_∞(Z); Z_p) the Z_p-span of Pontryagin products x_1·x_2 and of β(x′_1·x′_2) for mod-p^k classes, KSp_i(Z) ⊗ Z_p → H_i(Sp_∞(Z); Z_p)_Ind is an isomorphism for 1 ≤ i ≤ 2p − 2; hence for p > 2k, KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) is a Galois-equivariant quotient of H_{4k−2}(Sp_∞(Z); Z_p).
items.note: An instance of Theorem 8.4.

items.name: Theorem 8.1: divisibility of Chern numbers of families over Q
items.statement: Let A → X be a principally polarized abelian scheme over a smooth projective complex variety X of dimension n, defined over Q, with Hodge bundle ω, and n = n_1 + … + n_r with all n_i odd. Then s_n(A/X) = ∫_X ch_{n_1}(ω) ⋯ ch_{n_r}(ω) is divisible by every prime p > max_j(n_j) for which p divides the numerator of B_{n_i+1} for some i. For one part (n = 2k − 1): p > 2k and p | numerator of ζ(1 − 2k) imply p | numerator of c_H([S]) (1.5).
items.note: Stated as corrected: the paper allows p = max_j(n_j), where its integrality step fails (sourceIssues). The proof splits (8.1) and contradicts Theorem 7.8 via (8.2), Theorem 3.5 and Kolster–Nguyen Quang Do–Fleckinger Cor. 4.2.

items.name: Γ-spaces and Segal's infinite loop space machine
items.statement: A Γ-space is a functor Γ^op → sSets_* (Γ^op a skeleton of finite pointed sets) with X({∗}) contractible; its prolongation to sSets_* gives the connective spectrum B^∞X with spaces |X(S^n)| (A.1)–(A.2); X is special if X(S ∨ T) → X(S) × X(T) is a weak equivalence, and then (Segal) B^∞X is an Ω-spectrum and |X(S^0)| → Ω^∞B^∞X is a group completion (A.3)–(A.4); there is a natural map Σ^∞_+|X(S^0)| → B^∞X (A.5), and S ↦ S ∧ M_+ gives Σ^∞_+M (Example A.3).
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Definitions A.1–A.2, (A.1)–(A.5), Example A.3, pp. 300–303
items.note: StableHomotopyKTheory H.4 plans group completion via Segal Γ-spaces and H.5 spectra. Definition A.1 asks for X({∗}) to be a point, which the paper's own examples do not satisfy (sourceIssues).

items.name: Γ-space models for K(R) and KSp(Z)
items.statement: S ↦ N(𝒫_S(R)), with 𝒫_S(R) the groupoid of pairs (n, φ : R^S → M_n(R)) and R^S-linear isomorphisms, is a special Γ-space whose spectrum models K(R) and whose map (A.4) models |𝒫(R)| → Ω^∞K(R) (Example A.4); S ↦ N(SP_S(Z)), adding a symplectic form for which Z^S acts by symmetric endomorphisms, models KSp(Z) with infinite loop space Z × BSp_∞(Z)^+ (Example A.5).

items.name: Betti realization of simplicial complex varieties
items.statement: For quasi-projective X over C and compact Hausdorff Δ, morphisms Spec(C^Δ) → X over C correspond to continuous maps Δ → X(C)^an (Lemma A.7; C^Δ the continuous functions), so Sing_n(X(C)) = X(C^{Δ^n}); for a simplicial complex variety (or functor from C-algebras to simplicial sets) X, Sing^an(X) is the diagonal of ([n], [m]) ↦ X_m(C^{Δ^n}) (Definition A.8). For a smooth surjection U → V the Čech nerve U_• has Sing^an(U_•) ≃ Sing^an(V) (Example A.10).
items.locator: Appendix A.2.1, Lemma A.7, Definition A.8, pp. 305–307; A.3, Example A.10, p. 311
items.note: Lemma A.7 is stated for any scheme but the analytic topology was defined only for quasi-projective ones.

items.name: The p-completed étale homotopy type Et_p and the comparison with Betti realization
items.statement: For a simplicial variety X, Friedlander's rigid étale homotopy type (hypercovers U_{•,•}, diagonal [n] ↦ π_0(U_{n,n}), indexed by HRR(X)) followed by Bousfield–Kan pro-p completion into p-finite simplicial sets and holim defines a simplicial set Et_p(X) (A.9)–(A.10), functorial for all field automorphisms σ of C (A.7), with H^*_et(X; F_p) → H^*(Et_p(X); F_p) an isomorphism when the domain is finite-dimensional in each degree and vanishes in degree 1 (Lurie, DAG XIII); a zig-zag Sing^an(X) ← holim_U Sing^an(U) → Et_p(X) (A.2.3), natural for continuous σ, induces the Artin comparison on mod-p cohomology.
items.note: Property (iii) needs finite-dimensional mod-p cohomology in each degree, which fails for the infinite coproducts used in A.5 (sourceIssues).

items.name: Betti realization of 𝒜_g and the Aut(C)-action on BSp_{2g}(Z)^∧_p
items.statement: For the simplicial variety X_g of an atlas U → 𝒜_g (e.g. 𝒜_g(N) → 𝒜_g, N ≥ 4, a Borel construction for Sp_{2g}(Z/N)), Sing^an(X_g) ≃ BSp_{2g}(Z), products 𝒜_g × 𝒜_{g′} → 𝒜_{g+g′} matching orthogonal sum (Example A.11); on 0-simplices Sing^an_0(X_g) ≃ N(𝒜_g(C)) ≃ ℍ_g^δ//Sp_{2g}(Z) (A.11), so (A.6) models |N𝒜_g(C)| → BSp_{2g}(Z) → BSp_{2g}(Z)^∧_p Aut(C)-equivariantly (Example A.12).

items.name: A Γ-object in simplicial schemes over Q modelling KSp(Z)
items.statement: For finite pointed T, 𝒜(T) classifies principally polarized (A, ℒ, φ : Z^T → End(A)) with Rosati-symmetric image, and (A, ℒ, φ) ↦ (A_t)_t gives 𝒜(T) ≃ (∐_g 𝒜_g)^{T∖∗} (A.12), functorial in T; rigidifying by projective embeddings gives quasi-projective U(T) (components of Hilbert schemes) and the Čech nerve Z(T). Proposition A.13: Sing^an(Spec C ×_Q Z(T)) ≃ N(SP_T(Z)) naturally in T, so Sing^an(Z(S^0)_C) ≃ ∐_g NSp_{2g}(Z); and Map(Spec C, Z(S^0)) ≃ ∐_g N(𝒜_g(C)) (A.13).

items.name: The spectrum-level Aut(C)-action on KSp(Z; Z_p) and Proposition 6.2
items.statement: For p > 3 (H^1(B Sp_{2g}(Z); F_p) = 0 and finite type), the comparison Sing^an(Z_C) → Et_p(Z_C) of Γ-spaces is a mod-p homology equivalence levelwise, so after smashing with Moore spaces M(Z/p^k, 2) one gets KSp(Z; Z_p) ≃ holim_k M(Z/p^k) ∧ B^∞(Et_p(Z ⊗_Q C)), on which Aut(C) acts by spectrum maps; the map π^s_n(Sing^an_0(Z(S^0)_C); Z/p^k) → KSp_n(Z; Z/p^k) is Aut(C)-equivariant, which is the commutativity of (6.2); for p ≤ 3 one smashes with the Moore space before taking Et_p (Remark A.14).
items.note: The componentwise definition of Et_p on infinite coproducts is needed here (sourceIssues).

routes.reason: M.7 plans étale K-theory, its descent theorems and the comparison range. Thomason's theorem — étale descent for Bott-inverted K-theory, with the spectral sequence H^{−s}_et(X; μ_q^{⊗t/2}) ⇒ K^{(β)}_{t+s}(X; Z/q), its Adams-operation equivariance and naturality for transfers — is that descent theorem in the form the paper uses.

N.6 plans the cohomological description of the K-theory of S-integers. Lemmas 2.11 and 2.14 (Bott-inverted K-theory of Z[1/p] and Z[ζ_q, 1/p] in all degrees, split by ψ^{−1} into H^0 and H^2 of twists of μ_q) are exactly such descriptions.

GN.6 plans higher Hermitian K-theory with its forgetful and hyperbolic maps and source-scoped periodicity. Karoubi's splitting of KSp(Z)[1/2] into K(Z)[1/2]^{(+)} and the Witt part, with the fibre sequence K(Z)_{hC_2} → KSp(Z) → τ_{≥0}L^{−s}(Z), is the instance the paper uses.

routes.title: Étale homotopy types and pro-spaces
routes.brief: This route coalesces with the EtaleHomotopyTypes roadmap proposed by PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 (same id, title and area) and adds the layers that Feng–Galatius–Venkatesh, Invent. Math. 230 (2022), Appendix A.2, need; everything else there is imported from the existing brief. Add: (1) Betti realization of simplicial complex varieties: for quasi-projective X over C and compact Hausdorff Δ, morphisms Spec(C^Δ) → X correspond to continuous maps Δ → X(C)^an (Lemma A.7), Sing^an(X)_n = X(C^{Δ^n}) with the diagonal for simplicial X (Definition A.8), and Čech nerves of smooth surjections U → V (V smooth) realize to Sing^an(V) (Example A.10). (2) The p-completed étale homotopy type as an honest simplicial set: Friedlander's rigid hypercovers giving an inverse system functorial in X (Friedlander, Étale homotopy of simplicial schemes), Bousfield–Kan pro-p completion into p-finite simplicial sets, and Et_p(X) := holim, with H^*_et(X; F_p) ≅ H^*(Et_p(X); F_p) when H^*_et is finite-dimensional in each degree and H^1 = 0 (Lurie, DAG XIII, Prop. 3.3.8 and Thm. 3.4.2); define Et_p componentwise on coproducts (source issue E14). (3) Functoriality of Et_p for all field automorphisms σ of C over the base-change of schemes over Q (so Aut(C) acts on Et_p(X_C)), and the natural zig-zag Sing^an(X) ← holim_U Sing^an(U) → Et_p(X), functorial for continuous σ, realizing Artin's comparison on mod-p cohomology. Tests: BZ/p as a simplicial scheme; a smooth projective curve; the coproduct ∐_N Spec C (where the non-componentwise definition fails). Consumers: ArithmeticKTheoryPartIISymplecticGaloisAction (Appendix A.3–A.5 of the same paper) besides the existing anabelian consumer.
routes.reason: PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 proposed EtaleHomotopyTypes as the atlas's home for étale homotopy theory and asked later arithmetic uses to import it. The Betti realization and the p-completed étale homotopy type Et_p with its comparison map are general étale-homotopy constructions, so they coalesce there rather than in the K-theory Part II.

routes.title: K-theory of number fields and S-integers, Part II: symplectic K-theory of Z and its Galois action
routes.brief: Plan the symplectic K-theory of Z and its Galois action, following Tony Feng, Soren Galatius and Akshay Venkatesh, The Galois action on symplectic K-theory, Invent. Math. 230 (2022), 225–319 (arXiv 2007.15078). The final theorems, as the paper states them: (1) Main theorem (Theorem 7.8): for odd p and k ≥ 1, c_H : KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) → Z_p(2k − 1) is surjective and Aut(C)-equivariant; Ker(c_H) ≅ K_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) is a finite p-group with trivial action; the action factors through Γ = Gal(H_{p^∞}/Q), and Ker(c_H) → KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z_p) → Z_p(2k − 1) is initial among extensions of Z_p(2k − 1) by trivial Γ-modules (with or without a ⟨c⟩-equivariant splitting), the kernel of the universal extension being H_1(Γ, ⟨c⟩; Z_p(2k − 1)). (2) Theorem 7.1 (mod q with Gal(H_q/Q)); Theorem 7.10 (the group G of the maximal extension unramified outside p, split over a decomposition group G_𝔭: the étale sheaf of KSp on Z[1/p] is the universal extension of Z_p(2k − 1) by a trivial sheaf split over Q_p); Theorem 7.14 (the same for Bott-inverted KSp^{(β)} and every k ∈ Z); §7.7 (trivial action on KSp_{4k−1}). (3) Theorem 3.5: KSp_i(Z; Z/q) ≅ K_i(Z; Z/q)^{(+)} ⊕ π_i(ku; Z/q)^{(−)} via (c_B, c_H). (4) Proposition 5.1: classes of CM abelian varieties with O_q-multiplication exhaust KSp_{4k−2}(Z; Z/q).
